title: Bikes and Cycling
goal: Explain what kind of bike you need, arrange a rental, and describe a problem without guessing a repair.

runs.text: A
commuter bike
is used for trips such as going to work. An
e-bike
has electric assistance. Your
budget
is the amount you intend to spend. Tell the salesperson about the trip, not only the bike's appearance.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: I'm looking for a bike for my commute.

turns.en: I'm looking for a bike for my commute.

turns.speaker: Salesperson

runs.text: How far do you ride, and what's your budget?

turns.en: How far do you ride, and what's your budget?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: About three miles each way. I'd like to stay under six hundred dollars.

turns.en: About three miles each way. I'd like to stay under six hundred dollars.

turns.speaker: Salesperson

runs.text: Will you carry it upstairs or take it on transit?

turns.en: Will you carry it upstairs or take it on transit?

runs.text: Upstairs, yes. Weight matters.

turns.speaker: Salesperson

runs.text: Would you like to try this one?

turns.en: Would you like to try this one?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Yes. Could you explain the gears first?

turns.en: Yes. Could you explain the gears first?

runs.text: “I mainly need it for getting around town” describes purpose. “I'd prefer something lighter” expresses a preference. “That's more than I want to spend” is a clear limit; it is not a personal attack on the salesperson.
Seat / saddle:
where you sit.
Handlebars:
the bars used to steer.
Pedals:
the parts pushed with your feet.
Chain:
the linked metal loop transmitting movement.
Gears:
parts that change the relationship between pedaling and wheel movement.
Brakes:
parts used to slow or stop.
Tire:
the outer part around a wheel;
spokes
connect the wheel's center and rim.
Light / battery / charger:
useful equipment words, especially when discussing an e-bike.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Can I rent a bike for two hours?

turns.en: Can I rent a bike for two hours?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Yes. Do you want a regular bike or an e-bike?

turns.en: Yes. Do you want a regular bike or an e-bike?

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: A regular bike. How do I unlock it?

turns.en: A regular bike. How do I unlock it?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: We unlock the bike for you here.

turns.en: We unlock the bike for you here.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: Where do I return it, and how do I know the rental has ended?

turns.en: Where do I return it, and how do I know the rental has ended?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Bring it back to this station. At the desk, we close the rental and give you a receipt marked “Returned.” That confirms the rental has ended.

turns.en: Bring it back to this station. At the desk, we close the rental and give you a receipt marked “Returned.” That confirms the rental has ended.

turns.speaker: Visitor

runs.text: So I need to bring it to the desk and get the marked receipt?

turns.en: So I need to bring it to the desk and get the marked receipt?

runs.text: Yes.

This is an invented rental service. “Can I leave it anywhere?” asks about a rule; it does not assume free parking. “Is a helmet available?” asks about equipment. App access, fees, and return rules vary.
What's up with the bike?

turns.speaker: Rider

runs.text: The front tire keeps going flat, and the brake feels loose.

turns.en: The front tire keeps going flat, and the brake feels loose.

runs.text: When did you notice that?

turns.speaker: Rider

runs.text: This morning. Could you check it?

turns.en: This morning. Could you check it?

blocks.caption: Report what you notice · Employee & Rider

runs.text: Here
What's up with the bike?

asks about a problem. It is not a greeting. Useful reports include “The chain came off,” “The light isn't working,” and “The battery won't charge.” Say “I don't know what's causing it” when you do not know. The lesson teaches reporting, not how to repair or safely operate a faulty bike.

Choose a role: commuter, three miles each way, stairs, $600 budget; or visitor, two-hour regular-bike rental. For this invented rental, staff unlock the bike at the station. Return it to that station’s desk; staff close the rental and give you a receipt marked “Returned.”
Explain your need. Partner asks about distance, budget, or bike type. Use the role details.

Ask the rental employee about unlocking and returning. Partner explains: “We unlock it for you here. Bring it back to this desk; we close the rental and give you a receipt marked ‘Returned.’” Confirm both the return location and the confirmation you should receive.
Report a flat front tire. Partner asks “When did it start?” Answer “This morning,” then request a check.
Solo: supply each customer turn after reading the employee's prompt, then swap roles. Later change one need or fault.
Possibilities:

“I need something light enough to carry upstairs.” “So I bring it back to this desk and get a receipt marked ‘Returned’?” “Could you check the front tire?” Check whether your purpose, limit, or observed fault is clear; a technical diagnosis is not required.
